name: Ch’an Po
bio: Ch’an Po is the spelling Giles uses for this poet of the 10th century AD. His poem here is a disillusioned official’s wish for peace.
The poems here are Herbert A. Giles’s versions in Chinese Poetry in English Verse (1898), given with the poet’s name as spelled in that book.

poems.title: Disillusioned
poems.author: Ch’an Po
poems.text:
For ten long years I plodded through the vale of lust and strife,
Then through my dreams there flashed a ray of the old sweet peaceful life

No scarlet-tasselled hat of state can vie with soft repose;
Grand mansions do not taste the joys that the poor man's cabin knows.
I hate the threatening clash of arms when fierce retainers throng,
I loathe the drunkard's revels and the sound of fife and song;
But I love to seek a quiet nook, and some old volume bring
Where I can see the wild flowers bloom and hear the birds in spring.
